tasks.name: Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures
Design highly available and/or fault-tolerant architectures

concepts.name: Stateful vs stateless; horizontal vs vertical scaling
concepts.description: Stateless tiers externalize request/session state. Horizontal scaling adds instances; vertical scaling makes one instance larger.

concepts.name: Load balancing with Auto Scaling
concepts.description: Elastic Load Balancing distributes requests across healthy targets, and EC2 Auto Scaling adjusts the number of instances to match demand.

concepts.name: Amazon SQS decoupling
concepts.description: SQS buffers work durably. Standard queues use at-least-once delivery, so visibility timeout, DLQ, and idempotent-consumer behavior matter.

concepts.name: Amazon SNS fan-out
concepts.description: Amazon SNS publishes one message to multiple subscribers or downstream endpoints through a topic.

concepts.name: Amazon EventBridge routing
concepts.description: Amazon EventBridge routes events from AWS services, custom applications, and partners to targets by matching event patterns.

concepts.name: AWS Step Functions
concepts.description: AWS Step Functions coordinates multi-step workflows with explicit states, branching, retries, timeouts, and service integrations.

concepts.name: Lambda serverless compute
concepts.description: AWS Lambda runs event-driven code without managing servers and scales concurrent execution in response to incoming work within service limits.

concepts.name: ECS, EKS, and Fargate
concepts.description: Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS orchestrate containers, while AWS Fargate supplies serverless container compute for supported ECS and EKS workloads.

concepts.name: API Gateway for loosely coupled APIs
concepts.description: Amazon API Gateway provides managed endpoints for REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs and integrates with backends such as Lambda or private services.

concepts.name: RDS Multi-AZ DB instance/cluster vs read replicas
concepts.description: Multi-AZ DB instance deployments provide HA with a non-readable standby; Multi-AZ DB clusters add readable standbys; read replicas primarily scale reads.

concepts.name: Availability Zones and Regions as failure domains
concepts.description: Availability Zones are isolated locations within a Region, and using multiple AZs reduces exposure to a single-AZ failure.

concepts.name: Route 53 health checks and failover
concepts.description: Amazon Route 53 routing policies can direct users among endpoints, and health-aware policies can stop returning unhealthy targets when configured appropriately.

concepts.name: Disaster recovery strategies and RPO/RTO
concepts.description: RPO measures tolerated data loss and RTO measures tolerated downtime. DR strategies trade steady-state cost for recovery characteristics.

concepts.name: Replication, backups, and durability
concepts.description: Replication improves availability or locality by maintaining additional copies, while backups preserve recoverable historical points.

concepts.name: RDS Proxy and database connection resilience
concepts.description: RDS Proxy pools and reuses database connections so bursty applications do not exhaust database connection capacity.

concepts.name: Immutable infrastructure and automated replacement
concepts.description: Immutable infrastructure replaces unhealthy or outdated instances from versioned images or templates instead of manually repairing servers in place.

concepts.name: Caching and edge acceleration
concepts.description: CloudFront caches content near viewers, ElastiCache provides general in-memory caching, and DAX accelerates DynamoDB reads.

concepts.name: Object, block, and file storage selection
concepts.description: S3 is object storage, EBS is block storage, and EFS provides managed shared file storage.

concepts.name: Service quotas, throttling, and failover capacity
concepts.description: Resilient designs need enough service-quota and request-rate headroom in every Region/account that can receive failover load.

concepts.name: AWS X-Ray workload visibility
concepts.description: X-Ray traces requests through distributed components and helps identify dependencies, latency, and errors.

questions.prompt: An order platform must absorb traffic bursts, notify several downstream consumers, and coordinate a multi-step fulfillment workflow. Choose the architecture decisions in sequence.

steps.prompt: Checkout producers must not fail just because workers temporarily slow down. What decouples the rates?

choices.label: Place durable work messages on SQS
Publish only to an SNS topic with no durable work queue
Add an ALB between producer and worker
Change Route 53 routing policy

steps.prompt: A completed order event must reach billing, analytics, and notification consumers independently.

choices.label: Publish the event through SNS fan-out, optionally to separate SQS queues
Have every consumer poll one database row
Use an Auto Scaling group as the message bus
Write one file to EFS and treat it as pub/sub

steps.prompt: Fulfillment has explicit charge → reserve inventory → ship steps with retries and branching.

choices.label: Model the orchestration in Step Functions
Use Route 53 failover
Use ElastiCache as the workflow engine
Use a security group rule for sequencing

steps.prompt: Which test most directly validates resilience?

choices.label: Burst producers while slowing a consumer; verify SQS backlog grows safely, consumers recover, and duplicate/error handling behaves as designed
Check only one Lambda CPU metric
Check the bill
